title: Private installer: migrate batching tier config + validation + rollback guidance
author: Diego Santos
body:
Context: runtime-1.21 introduces tiered batching defaults via `batching_tier` (fast|standard|cost_efficient). Hosted/Dedicated pick up defaults automatically, but Private customers commonly pin explicit batching knobs in values/config. This PR updates the private installer to (1) recognize the new tier config, (2) safely migrate older configs, (3) validate precedence (explicit knobs > tier), and (4) provide a clear rollback path if the rollout is paused.

What changed (high level):
- Added support for `runtime.batching_tier` in the installer config model and rendered runtime config.
- Implemented a migration step for legacy configs:
  - If legacy explicit batching knobs are present (e.g., max_batch_size/max_queue_delay_ms/prefill_decode weights), we keep them unchanged and do NOT auto-infer or force a tier.
  - If no explicit batching knobs are present, we set `batching_tier` to `standard` ONLY when the feature flag is enabled (see below). Otherwise we omit the field and preserve existing behavior.
  - If `batching_tier` is present but invalid, we fail validation with a actionable error (allowed values + link to docs).
- Added precedence + “effective config” notes in the generated install report to reduce confusion during support escalations.
- Added validation rules:
  - Disallow setting `batching_tier` simultaneously with any explicit batching knob unless `runtime.allow_mixed_batching_config=true` (escape hatch for phased migration / advanced users). Default is false.
  - When `batching_tier=fast`, enforce `streaming=true` guardrails: we warn (not fail) if streaming routes are enabled with unusually high queue delay overrides.
- Added rollback instructions to the installer README and the post-install summary:
  - Rollback tier enablement via installer feature flag (and re-apply) OR remove `batching_tier` from config and re-apply.
  - Provided a one-liner to export the rendered runtime config before/after to make diffs explicit.

Feature flagging / rollout:
- Introduced `features.tiered_batching_defaults` (default: false) in the installer config.
- When disabled, installer will not inject a tier default. Customers can still explicitly set `runtime.batching_tier` if they want.
- When enabled, installer will set `runtime.batching_tier=standard` only for installs that do not already have explicit batching knobs.

Why the default is conservative:
- Avoid surprising behavior changes for existing Private deployments that tuned batching directly.
- Keep the runtime-side precedence model simple for customers: either pick a tier OR set explicit knobs.

Files / areas touched:
- installer/config/schema.yaml: added `runtime.batching_tier`, `features.tiered_batching_defaults`, and `runtime.allow_mixed_batching_config`.
- installer/migrate/migrations/2025_03_tiered_batching.py: migration logic from legacy batching configs.
- installer/validate/runtime_config.py: new validation + warnings.
- installer/render/runtime_config.tmpl: emit `batching_tier` when applicable.
- docs/private/upgrade-notes.md + docs/private/rollback.md: new sections for tier rollout.
- tests/: unit tests for migration/validation and a golden “rendered config” snapshot.

Test plan:
- Unit: migration tests for (a) legacy explicit knobs, (b) clean install with flag off, (c) clean install with flag on, (d) invalid tier, (e) mixed tier+explicit knobs.
- Snapshot: rendered runtime config includes/omits `batching_tier` as expected.
- Manual: local install dry-run:
  - `installer apply --dry-run --config ./examples/private-values.yaml` and inspect report output.

Operational notes:
- If a customer reports timeouts after enabling cost_efficient tier, support should confirm whether they have explicit batching overrides in place, and whether the tier flag was injected by installer or explicitly set. The install report now prints (1) whether the tier was defaulted and (2) which explicit knobs are present.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Align with helm chart values naming (tracked in redwood-helm-charts PR) to ensure config fields map 1:1.
- Add a small CLI helper to print “effective batching config” from a live cluster (planned for runtime control-plane; separate repo).

Screenshots/log excerpts (dry-run summary):
- "tiered_batching_defaults enabled: true"
- "runtime.batching_tier: standard (defaulted by installer)"
- "validation: OK (no explicit batching knobs detected)"

Release note:
- Private installer now supports `runtime.batching_tier` and includes migration + validation. Default behavior is unchanged unless `features.tiered_batching_defaults=true` is enabled.

Co-authored-by: Connor O'Brien (doc wording + rollback steps)
commits: config: add batching_tier + tiered batching feature flag to schema
migrate: add tiered batching migration step (legacy batching knobs detection)
validate: enforce tier value enum + mixed-config guardrail
render: emit batching_tier to runtime config when applicable
docs: add upgrade + rollback instructions for tiered batching
review_conversation:
Ethan Park: Can we avoid silently choosing a tier for existing installs? I’m worried about implicit behavior changes for regulated customers.
Diego Santos: Agree — migration only injects `standard` when `features.tiered_batching_defaults=true` AND no explicit batching knobs exist. Otherwise we leave untouched.

Rafael Mendes: Please add a clear rollback procedure and make sure the installer prints whether the tier was defaulted or user-specified.
Diego Santos: Added docs/private/rollback.md and a post-install summary line that includes "(defaulted by installer)" vs "(user-specified)".

Benji Okafor: The mixed config guardrail is good, but I’d prefer fail-fast (error) over warning when both tier + explicit knobs are present.
Diego Santos: Implemented as validation error by default. Added `runtime.allow_mixed_batching_config=true` escape hatch for phased migrations / internal testing.

Allison Grant: For the fast tier warning, can we ensure it’s a warning and not a hard failure? Some customers set queue delay higher intentionally.
Diego Santos: Kept as warning only; validation message points to docs and explains streaming cadence risk.
